title: Search Insert Position
interviewTips: Ask if array is sorted ascending and has distinct values - this confirms binary search lower_bound applies
Trade-off: linear scan is simpler but O(n); binary search gives O(log n) with same O(1) space and is expected
Edge-case tip: handle target smaller than all elements (return 0) and larger than all (return n); verify loop invariant and mid overflow avoidance

approaches.name: Approach 1: Linear Scan
approaches.intuition: Since array is sorted, the answer is the first index i where nums[i] >= target. Scan left to right and return that i, otherwise return n.
approaches.theory: Sorted order guarantees all elements before the first >= target are < target and all after are > target. This is exactly the lower_bound definition. Linear scan checks each element once, so it finds the insertion point in order. If no element satisfies nums[i] >= target, target is larger than all elements and belongs at the end (index n).

timeComplexity.explanation: We visit each element at most once in worst case when target is larger than all elements.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only index variable used, no extra storage.

edgeCases: single element array: returns 0 or 1 correctly

approaches.name: Approach 2: Binary Search Lower Bound
approaches.intuition: Because array is sorted, we can discard half the search space per step. Maintain candidate answer ans=n and shrink [left, right] to find first position with nums[mid] >= target.
approaches.theory: Classic lower_bound binary search. Invariant: answer lies in [left, right+1]. Let mid=(left+right)/2. If nums[mid] >= target, mid is a valid candidate, so set ans=mid and search left half right=mid-1. Else nums[mid] < target, answer must be to the right, so left=mid+1. Loop ends when left>right and ans is the smallest index with nums[ans] >= target, or n if none. Halving each iteration gives logarithmic time.

timeComplexity.explanation: Search space halves each iteration, at most log2(n)+1 comparisons.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only left, right, mid, ans pointers used.

edgeCases: target present e.g. 5 returns its index 2
n=1: works for target smaller, equal, larger
